precepts.text: The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord; he turns rulers whithersoever he will, no matter who is voted in.
precepts.point: The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the thing that hath been is that which shall be. That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon, and of the Greeks, because these things must come to pass.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
“I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants, that I might shew these my signs before him”. The Most High hardened Pharaoh and his servants so that he might show his signs and exemplify his power in the earth, and after he brought down Egypt and delivered the people, every nation feared Israel and the God of Israel.

He could do that because Pharaoh's heart was his to turn. “The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.” He is in control of the mind of the kings of the world. So there is no need to worry over who becomes president or who gets put in office; either way the Most High is in control.

The same holds in spiritual Egypt today. He will harden the hearts of the rulers of this kingdom so they will not let Israel go and will continue to oppress. It does not matter who is voted into office; whoever sits in the seat, the Most High turns him about like the rivers of water.

precepts.text: He has mercy on whom he will have mercy; Pharaoh was raised up for this same purpose, that the Most High might show his power in him.
precepts.point: The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the thing that hath been is that which shall be. That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon, and of the Greeks, because these things must come to pass.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
Paul goes right back to this moment. “For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion. So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.” And then Pharaoh: “For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.”

That is why the Lord hardened his heart. Pharaoh was raised up for this same purpose, so that the Most High could show his power in him and have his name declared throughout all the earth. After Egypt was brought down and the people delivered, every nation feared Israel and the God of Israel; the name was declared.

“Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth.” The hardening of Pharaoh was not Pharaoh's doing. The Most High hardens whom he will, as he had mercy on Israel.

precepts.text: The potter has power over the clay to make one vessel unto honour and another unto dishonour; the vessels of wrath were fitted to destruction.
precepts.point: The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the thing that hath been is that which shall be. That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon, and of the Greeks, because these things must come to pass.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
The next question is the one a man asks: if the Lord hardened Pharaoh, “Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will?” Paul answers, “O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?”

The potter has power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour and another unto dishonour. Some nations are honourable, which are the Israelites, and some are dishonourable. Pharaoh and Egypt were the vessel unto dishonour, made from the same lump.

“What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”. The vessels of wrath were fitted to destruction and endured with much longsuffering so that the Most High could show how powerful he is. That is why Pharaoh was raised up and hardened: so that bringing him down would make the power of God known before him and before all the earth.

precepts.text: Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated; Jacob is the honourable vessel and Esau the dishonourable.
precepts.point: The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the thing that hath been is that which shall be. That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon, and of the Greeks, because these things must come to pass.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
“As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” This names the two vessels. Jacob is the honourable vessel and Esau the dishonourable: some nations are honourable, which are the Israelites, and some are dishonourable, of the same lump.

The vessels of wrath are fitted to destruction and endured with much longsuffering so that the Most High can show how powerful he is. That is why Esau had to be set on such a high level, as Pharaoh was raised up: so that when he brings these people down, all will know God is truly all powerful. Pharaoh hardened in Egypt and Esau exalted today are the same thing, a vessel of wrath lifted up so that the power of God is shown in bringing it down.

That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon, and of the Greeks, because these things must come to pass.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The hardening of Pharaoh's heart was written down for us. The history of Egypt teaches this captivity.

That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon and of the Greeks. What the Most High did with Pharaoh, hardening him so he would not let Israel go, he does with the rulers of spiritual Egypt today. So we read Egypt to understand where we are, and we take hope from it: the Most High brought Israel out then, and he is in control now.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” What was done in Egypt is what shall be done. The Most High hardened Pharaoh's heart and the hearts of his servants so they would not let Israel go; he will harden the hearts of the rulers of this kingdom the same way.

That is why the captivities repeat their patterns, and why this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon and of the Greeks. These things must come to pass; there is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.text: In their affliction they will seek me early; the oppression is used to wake the people up.
precepts.point: The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the thing that hath been is that which shall be. That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon, and of the Greeks, because these things must come to pass.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
Why would the Most High harden the rulers so they continue to oppress Israel? “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” The oppression is used to wake the people up. In the affliction the people will seek him early, acknowledge their offence and seek his face.

So in spiritual Egypt today he hardens the hearts of the rulers of this kingdom so they will not let Israel go, and the affliction drives the people to him. Pharaoh's hardened heart showed the signs of the Most High before Egypt; the hardened hearts of these rulers bring Israel back to seek his face.

precepts.text: No more Blessed be the Lord that brought Israel out of Egypt, but out of the land of the north; the greater exodus is still ahead.
precepts.point: The same deliverance will be told again: it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, but, The Lord liveth that brought them up from the land of the north, out of Babylon the Great where the people sit today.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
“that thou mayest tell in the ears of thy son, and of thy son’s son, what things I have wrought in Egypt”: that is what Israel does every year at the Passover, giving honour to the things he did in Egypt and the way he delivered the people out of the hand of the oppressors.

But the telling of Egypt is not the last telling. “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt; But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them: and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.”

The greater exodus is still ahead. The people sit today in the land of the north, in Babylon the Great, and the Lord will bring them up from there and from all the lands where he drove them, back into the land he gave their fathers. Then what the fathers tell their sons will be that deliverance, and by it the sons will know how that he is the Lord.

precepts.text: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity; the feasts gather the nation.
precepts.point: Pharaoh offered to let only the men go, and Moses and Aaron were driven out from his presence.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
Pharaoh asked who would go, and Moses answered, “We will go with our young and with our old, with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we must hold a feast unto the Lord.” Not the men only, as Pharaoh offered: everyone, young and old, sons and daughters, flocks and herds.

“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” The Most High loves to see Israel gathered together in unity. That is why so many feast days bring the nation together to honour him: a feast unto the Lord is the whole nation, and Moses would not hold one with half of it left in Egypt. Pharaoh said “go now ye that are men”, and Moses and Aaron were driven out from his presence.

precepts.text: God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie; Pharaoh was deceived into thinking he could threaten the servant of God.
precepts.point: Moses answered, Thou hast spoken well, I will see thy face again no more.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
After the rivers turned to blood, the hail with flaming fire, the locusts and the darkness, Pharaoh still thought he was in a position to give out threats: “see my face no more; for in that day thou seest my face thou shalt die.” Egypt was destroyed around him, and he threatened the servant of God with death.

That is the deceivableness of the strong delusion. “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie”. God sends it. The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and Pharaoh believed a lie: that he could still threaten Moses.

The same delusion falls on Israel when the people go reprobate in their sins: believing the Sabbath begins when the sun comes up, that anything can be eaten on Passover, or that the leaven to be put away is only the heart. Sin blinds, whether it is Pharaoh or Israel. Moses answered, “Thou hast spoken well, I will see thy face again no more.”

points: Tomorrow will I bring the locusts into thy coast, and they shall eat the residue of that which is escaped, which remaineth unto you from the hail. The locusts eat all the crops. This plague goes into farming.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: The locusts would cover the face of the earth so no one could see the ground, eat the residue that escaped the hail, and fill the houses of Pharaoh, of his servants, and of all the Egyptians, such as neither their fathers nor their fathers' fathers had seen.

points: When the judgment got real, Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste and confessed, I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you. Everything had been eaten by the locusts, and now he begged that this death only be taken from him.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: Moses entreated the Lord, and a mighty strong west wind took away the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea; there remained not one locust in all the coasts of Egypt.

points: Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven, and there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days, even darkness which may be felt. They saw not one another, neither rose any from his place.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: But all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings; the Most High put a difference between his people and the Egyptians.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs
